summary: Tested the PIPEDA customer data requests (lookup, export, erase), the pharmacy pickup check-in, and the merchant batch rate tracker, on both backend and UI. New pytest suite: 16/16 pass. Regression suites test_rx_handoff_batch_alerts, test_pickup_run_geofence and test_privacy_compliance: 44/44 pass (run with -n 0). UI on a 390x844 viewport: admin lookup, export download, erase (409 and success) and the request log work; the driver PICKED UP -> count -> CONFIRM flow works; the merchant tracker shows progress, countdown and the pickup line. One HIGH logic bug was reproduced: the merchant never sees the pickup check-in once the run's cut-off has passed. Pickup always happens after cut-off, so in real use the tracker's pickup line never shows. Smaller issues: the merchant's 'expected' parcel count does not match the driver's 'drops' count, the photo file is not deleted on erase, and the erase confirm box carries over to a new lookup.

critical.issue: runs_today() moves a run to tomorrow's date as soon as its cut-off passes (afternoon 13:30, evening 16:30). merchant_detail looks up the pickup for that run's date, but pickups happen after cut-off (14:00-14:30 and 17:00-17:30). So the pickup is always looked up on tomorrow's manifest and runs[].pickup is null at the time of real check-ins. batch-tracker-{run}-pickup ('PICKED UP ... ON TIME') never shows outside tests that check in before cut-off. Reproduced with /app/backend/tests/repro_iter34_cutoff_rollover.py: a check-in for today's afternoon run at 13:48 gives pickup None (run date 2026-10-27). The check-in only appears in recent_pickups, which the frontend does not use.

minor.issue: 'expected' counts every stop in the manifest (count_documents by manifest_id), but the driver card's 'drops' (and the prefilled count) counts only stops on this route. Reproduced: driver confirmed 1/1 with a green 'PICKUP CHECKED IN' toast, while the merchant saw 'PICKED UP · 1/2 PARCELS'. This happens whenever a manifest has stops that are not dispatched or are on another route. Also, the first route to check in blocks the others (unique manifest_id), so a manifest split across 2 routes cannot be fully checked in.
pod_photo_path is set to None, but the stored photo file is never deleted from storage, so the proof photo stays on disk/object storage after a PIPEDA erasure. The same applies to retention.

The export token can be reused for 5 minutes (not single-use) and is sent in the URL query, where proxy logs can capture it. data_requests.by is the user id for exports but the email for erasures (inconsistent audit field).
on_time is only 'now <= window end of the manifest date'. Checking in a day early, or before the pickup window opens, still counts as ON TIME.

ui_bugs.issue: The confirm state is not reset on a new lookup. If an admin opens the erase box for customer A and types ERASE, then searches customer B, the box stays open with ERASE already typed, so one tap erases B. Fix: call setConfirm(null) inside lookup().

integration_issues.issue: After the run's cut-off (always true at real pickup time) the tracker switches to tomorrow's run and the pickup line never shows (see backend critical).

issues: Times mix 24h and 12h. Check-in time is '13:47' (fmtDepotTime uses en-GB), but the pickup window and cut-off use '5:00 PM'. The spec example says 'PICKED UP 5:03 PM'.
Plurals: '1 PARCELS' on the driver card, 'ERASED 1 ORDERS' toast, '1 orders' in the request log and erase warning.
Retention card 'N ERASED' also goes up after customer-request erasures (it showed 2 and then 3 after the UI erasures), which mixes them with retention erasures.

action_items: HIGH: Make the merchant tracker show the pickup for the run that is currently being picked up. Option 1: in merchant_detail, also look up today's manifest pickup (f'{mid}:{today}:{key}') when the run has moved to tomorrow, and return it as e.g. last_pickup. Option 2: keep showing today's run until its pickup window ends, then show tomorrow's. Option 3: render recent_pickups in the portal.

Make the driver 'drops' and the merchant 'expected' counts agree. Either count expected per route, or show the driver the manifest total ('1 of 2 parcels on your route'). Decide what happens when a manifest is split across routes, since the unique manifest_id check-in blocks the second route.
CustomerDataRequests: call setConfirm(null) when a new lookup starts.
erase_stops: delete the stored photo file (pod_photo_path) before clearing the field.
Optional: make the export token single-use (store its jti in data_requests), use a consistent 'by' field, use one time format (12h) on the pickup/tracker lines, and fix plurals.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 5,200 lines; split the privacy/customer-requests and pharmacy pickup code into modules.
pickup_window_end splits manifest_id on ':' with no validation. It is only reached after the stop lookup succeeds, so it is safe for now.
PickupCheckIn uses testID pickup-{run}. Two pharmacies on the same run on one route would give duplicate testIDs; use the manifest id.

conftest.py: on teardown it restores driver consent to the earlier state, which races under xdist (-n auto). A parallel run gave a false 403 'Accept the privacy & compliance terms'. Run the new suite with -n 0.

success_rate.backend: 100% of the 16 new tests and 44 regression tests (plus 1 HIGH logic bug found by repro)
success_rate.frontend: ~90% (all flows work; the tracker pickup line will not show after cut-off in real use)

UI prep: python tests/ui_seed_pickup_run.py setup|cleanup (pending pharmacy stop on drv-1's route) and python tests/prep_ui_iter34.py setup|cleanup (closed-order customer +15195550976 for erase). Regression suites deliver MD1006, so check its status before using +15195550105 for a 409 test, or reset first. Tests check in before the evening cut-off (16:30 Toronto); after cut-off, runs[].pickup will be null (known bug).
rca_of_issue: Tracker pickup missing: runs_today() picks the run date with now < cutoff, otherwise tomorrow. merchant_detail uses that date to look up db.pickups. The pickup window always starts after the cut-off, so a real check-in is written to today's manifest_id while the portal is already looking at tomorrow's. Repro: tests/repro_iter34_cutoff_rollover.py. Fix: also look up today's manifest pickup, or keep showing today's run until its pickup window ends.
